Anything more than half beneath it is caught unless it rolls its Initiative or less on a D6, and what is caught takes an S6 hit that no armour will stop. Vehicles and buildings are caught automatically, and either one halts the bolt where it stands. Otherwise the template advances 12" along the same line at the start of every later psychic phase. It stays in play until the Warlock takes the card back into hand during a psychic phase, until the Warlock dies, until it is nullified, or until it finally passes off the table.

Lightning leaps from the psyker's hands up to 24" and takes the first model in its path with an S6 hit that does D3 wounds rather than 1. Should that model die, the bolt jumps to anything within 6" of it for another S6 hit and D3 wounds, and again from there, to six hits in all. Where it penetrates a vehicle's armour it may jump likewise: to another model within 6", or to a different location on the same vehicle, up to the same six.

A column of fire erupts from the ground and swallows everything around it. The 2" radius Hellfire template is placed anywhere on the table within 24" of the psyker to mark the burning ground. Every model the template touches takes an S4 hit. The template may be left where it is, in which case it blocks line of sight and deals an S4 hit to anything that touches it. Left in place it lasts until nullified, or until the power is cast again.

Something huge and unseen takes hold of one model within 24" and knocks it about. The caster may shift that model up to 6" in any direction and set its facing as they like—into hand-to-hand combat, onto a blast marker, into dangerous ground, anywhere the terrain does not simply bar. A model handled this way is shaken out of overwatch. A vehicle cannot be moved by it, but one already moving loses control in its next movement phase on a D6 roll of 4, 5 or 6.

The Librarian looks a little way ahead and sees how things will fall out. From the moment the power is used until the next psychic phase opens, any failed roll of theirs may be taken again—to hit, damage, armour saves, Leadership tests and the rest.

One friendly squad, or one friendly model, is wrapped in energy, vanishes, and comes back somewhere else a moment later. The distance is up to 3D6" in whatever direction the caster likes, and nothing lying between—models, buildings, scenery, obstacles of any kind—has any bearing on it. A rooftop, a crag or any other high place is a legitimate destination. Troops set down in hand-to-hand combat join the fighting from the next round and count as having charged for that first one. Enemy models cannot be shifted by it.

The Weirdboy lets the Waaagh! out, and it goes everywhere at once. Every enemy psyker in range is thrown down and takes 1 wound if the Ork player beats their mastery level on a D6. A psyker put down that way works no further power until the next psychic phase, though warp cards remain available for nullifying and the like. Meanwhile every Ork and Gretchin unit within 36" of the Weirdboy gains +1 WS and may reroll any Ld test, until the end of the next turn.

Cast by the Librarian on themself or any model within 3". Psychic force floods through the subject: Toughness and Strength both double, to a ceiling of 10, while Move is halved, rounding up. Fighting is otherwise unaffected. The subject also gains an extra save on 4, 5 or 6, rolled before its ordinary armour save; weapon save modifiers do not touch it and it applies to every wound however caused, psychic powers included. Iron Arm holds for the remainder of the game unless nullified or the subject is slain, and only one model may be under it at a time.

The Warlock enters the mind of one Eldar within 12" and aims for them. That model fires at once, at up to twice the weapon's usual range, and the shot hits without a roll—pick the target and work out damage as normal. A pistol or basic weapon costs one card; ancient, heavy and support weapons cost two. Only the single shot is granted, so sustained fire and multiple shots alike yield one hit.

A bolt tears out of the Weirdboy's sloping brow and crosses up to 24" of battlefield dead straight. The first model it meets is filled with more Ork power than it can hold and must roll under its Toughness on a D6 or its head bursts, which kills it outright whatever its wounds. No armour save applies. Against a vehicle the bolt strikes one crew member at random, who rolls as above.

The psyker opens a gate through the warp. Take the two special Gate markers and place them anywhere within 18" of the psyker. The two markers represent either end of a tunnel through reality. Any models which move into one of the Gate markers disappear, instantaneously reappearing out of the other Gate marker. Models expend no movement being transported between the Gate markers and may charge or make run moves through them as normal. Only models small enough to get through the Gate may use it, so no vehicles etc can pass through. The Gate remains in play until it is nullified or the psyker using it is killed.

The Librarian creates an accelerated time field around themselves or another model within 3", making it seem that the subject speeds up to a blur while everything else barely moves. The subject doubles its Movement, Initiative, and Attacks characteristics as long as Quickening is in play and can fire twice in the shooting phase if they don't run or charge in the movement phase. Once used, Quickening remains in play until nullified or the Librarian is killed. Quickening may be used on only one model at a time.

The Librarian draws upon their inner reserves of strength to fortify themselves and those about them against psychic attack. Psychic attacks against the Librarian or any models within 6" of them are automatically nullified unless they roll higher than the Librarian's mastery level on a D6. Strength of Mind remains in play until it is nullified or the Librarian is killed.

A ball of absolute dark opens between the psyker's hands and spreads into a turning vortex. It can be sent off in any direction, and ruins whatever it meets. Use the Vortex template to show where it is, moving the template to trace its course. It travels 3D6" straight away, and whatever it touches suffers as though touched by a Vortex grenade. From the start of each turn after that, roll on the Vortex chart exactly as for the grenade. It lasts until nullified, until it disperses, or until it leaves the table.

Cast anywhere within 24" of the Ancestor Lord: a great shell of energy comes up out of the ground, and the special Dome template is placed within range. Nothing crosses its edge, so whatever was inside stays inside. Nothing sees, shoots or works a psychic power through it either. A model touching the dome may try to break it at the end of its own movement phase by rolling under its Strength on 3D6; a vehicle does the same on 2D6 against its Ram Value. Otherwise the dome stands until nullified or removed.

A curse laid on the machine spirits of the enemy. Place the 2" radius Machine Curse template anywhere within 24" of the psyker; everything even partly beneath it is caught. No ranged weapon in that area will fire, pistols in close combat included, and no robot, Terminator, Dreadnought or vehicle will move, until the curse is broken. Carry something out of the area and it works again. Troops may shoot into or through the area freely. The curse holds until nullified or until the psyker dies.

Raw warp energy, aimed by the Chaos Magus at one living model within 24". The victim resists by rolling its Toughness or less on 2D6. Failing that, the flesh gives: it becomes a Chaos Spawn and lurches 2D6" away in a random direction at once, keeping the Toughness and wounds it had. Thereafter it wanders 2D6" at random in each of its own compulsory movement phases, passing straight over anything in the way and dealing an automatic S4 hit to every model it touches. A Spawn never fights in hand-to-hand combat and is struck automatically by anyone who attacks it. Nothing breaks it and no psychology affects it. Even a nullify will not give it its old shape back.

Corrupting power turned on one enemy squad or model within 24". Each victim rolls its Ld or less on 2D6 to shrug it off. Whoever fails begins to caper and shriek with delight, and can do nothing else: no moving, no shooting, and no attack dice at all in hand-to-hand combat. The dance goes on until the power is nullified, until its caster dies, or until the caster chooses to end it.

A rotten wind loosed at one living enemy model within 24". It deals 3D6 hits less the target's Toughness, and each hit wounds on a D6 roll of 4+. Every 3 wounds it inflicts raises a Plaguebearer, and the new arrivals form a unit within 3" of what the wind killed.

The Chaos Magus draws a reeking cloud about themself and wears it. Any living model coming within 6" takes an S3 hit the moment it is close enough. Nurgle's followers and daemons walk through it untouched. It holds until nullified, until the Magus dies, or until the Magus lets it disperse.

The Librarian brightens, flares, and is gone. They reappear up to 4D6" off, arriving as another glow that flashes and fades. Arriving in hand-to-hand combat is allowed: they fight normally from the next round and count as charging in the first.

The Farseer reads the odds and picks out the line of action that serves one Eldar squad or vehicle best. That squad or vehicle adds 1 to every shooting to hit roll and to its Combat Scores in close combat. The card returns to the Farseer's hand at the opening of the next psychic phase, and may be played again. Farseer Only

The Librarian raises a shield of psychic force around themself. Any wound they take thereafter from shooting or close combat may be absorbed, one D6 per wound, on a roll of 3 or better. Against a psychic power that wounds or kills outright the shield saves on 4, 5 or 6, and a save made that way breaks the shield at once. Otherwise it stands until nullified or until the Librarian is killed.

The Chaos Magus gathers raw magic and throws it up to 12", to strike the first model in its way. That model must roll its Toughness or less on 2D6 to hold out; failing that, the magic tears through it, and it grows and alters and comes apart until nothing is left but slime. Armour is no defence. A vehicle takes a randomly allocated hit with an armour penetration of 3D6+6.

A wave of raw power thrown up to 24", catching the first model in its way and flinging it back D6+1". Anything it collides with stops the move dead, and both models take an S5 hit. It works on area templates as well—Vortex, Hellfire, plasma bursts and their like—and a template shoved this way scores a hit on everything it crosses.

A screaming wind of psychic force that picks troops up and throws them. Put the Eldritch Storm template anywhere within 24" of the Warlock, then roll a Scatter Dice for each model more than half beneath it. An arrow throws that model to the edge of the storm, and it may neither move nor shoot next turn; a hit does the same and adds an S4 hit on the way. Any vehicle caught inside goes out of control the next time it moves. Leave the card beside the Warlock, or face up at the table edge, to show the storm is up. It stands until the Warlock dies or ends it, and while it stands nothing sees, moves or shoots through it.

Psychic force breaks out of the Weirdboy's eyes as a shining wave. Set the Death Wave template with its centre touching the Weirdboy, then run it 4D6" in a straight line away. Whatever the template passes over is hit; a model only partly covered is hit on a D6 roll of 4, 5 or 6. Roll a D6 for each model hit—equal its Toughness or better and it dies, whatever its armour and however many wounds it had. Vehicles themselves are untouched, but each crew member is hit on a D6 roll of 5 or 6. Nothing stops the wave: models, scenery and buildings alike are simply passed through, and it carries on whether or not it did any harm. It travels another 4D6" the same way at the start of every later psychic phase, and stays in play until nullified or until it runs off the table.

The Librarian draws on the terrifying legends of Chapter history to create a monstrous spectral creature. The manifestation shoots forwards, crackling and spitting as it burns a trail of destruction in its path. The player draws a line 5D6" from the Librarian. Every model crossed by the line suffers one S5 hit causing 1 wound. Any squad suffering one or more casualties from the Salamander must take a Break test.

Cancels a psychic power anywhere on the table, whether it is being cast or already in play. Roll a dice: 1 to 3 and the attempt fails, 4 to 6 and it succeeds. Subtract 1 if the enemy Psyker is of higher Mastery Level, add 1 if they are lower, and subtract 2 if the army contains no Psykers at all. It has no power over another warp card.
Played as a psychic power is cast, and worth three force cards by itself. Nothing can nullify, reflect or destroy that power for the turn it is cast.

Played in place of a psychic power at any point in the psychic phase, and the phase stops there. Every warp card in either hand is discarded, even those that could otherwise be held back, and every psychic power in play fails at once.

Answers an enemy Psyker's power, which fails outright. Something comes through after them: roll a dice, add the enemy Psyker's Mastery Level and subtract the force cards they spent. On a modified result of 1 to 3 a daemon takes them. Grey Knights and Ork Weirdboyz are hardier, and fall only on a 6.

Held in hand until needed, and answers a power aimed at a friendly Psyker or any model within 6" of one, the Psyker included. The power fails. Both players then roll a dice in secret, adding one for each force card they give up. The higher total wins: if it is the defender's, the power is lost to the enemy for the rest of the battle; if not, it returns to their hand as usual.

Names one enemy Psyker and one friendly Psyker, who then contest. Each player rolls a dice and adds the chosen Psyker's Mastery Level. Whoever scores higher tears a power from the other's mind: one of the loser's powers is picked at random and discarded for the rest of the battle. A tie leaves both untouched.

Held in hand until needed. It answers a psychic power aimed at a friendly Psyker, or at any model standing within 6" of one. The power turns and travels 4D6" straight back along the line to its caster, crossing terrain without hindrance, and striking whatever eligible target it reaches first.

The Imperial Guard is the principal army of the Imperium, countless millions of soldiers fighting on thousands of worlds. Every world must offer a tenth of its armed forces for recruitment each year; the troops raised together form a regiment named for its home world. A regiment brings the uniforms and equipment of its own world, though nearly every Guardsman carries the lasgun. The Departmento Munitorium organises recruitment, supply and transport, and Commissars accompany every regiment to preserve discipline and loyalty. A Guard army takes months to assemble, and falls on the enemy with massed infantry, tanks and artillery.

The Space Marines of the Adeptus Astartes are the Imperium's elite, superhuman warriors created by gene-seed implants engineered from the genetic material of the Primarchs. They are organised into roughly a thousand Chapters, each an independent army of about a thousand warriors with its own fleet, traditions and recruiting grounds. Most Chapters follow the Codex Astartes, fighting in companies of ten squads; each squad takes the field in a Devastator, Assault or Tactical role. The Space Marines are far too few to garrison the Imperium, and are committed instead as shock troops, expected to stand their ground in any situation.

The Imperial Agents are the specialist armed bodies of the Imperium outside the Imperial Guard and the Space Marine Chapters. The Inquisition answers to itself alone, charged with finding and destroying any threat to humanity; the Grey Knights, a Chapter of daemon-hunting Space Marines, form the Chamber Militant of its Ordo Malleus. The Officio Assassinorum raises killers in hidden temples, and none below the High Lords of Terra may order one deployed. The Tech-Priests of the Adeptus Mechanicus guard the Imperium's ancient technology from Mars. These bodies seldom make war alone; their detachments fight beside Guard and Space Marine armies.

The Eldar are an ancient race whose worlds were destroyed when their ancestors surrendered wholly to their own desires. The survivors live aboard craftworlds, vast spacecraft adrift in deep space, and their numbers still decline. An Eldar lives for a thousand years and moves and thinks faster than any human; each masters one discipline, or path, at a time. Aspect Warriors train in shrines, each Aspect devoted to a different discipline of the war god Kaela Mensha Khaine. Every other Eldar can fight as a Guardian in the craftworld's defence, and Seers foretell the course of battle through psychic power.

The Orks are a savage green-skinned race found wherever humans have travelled, and love war above all else. Orks gather in tribes under the strongest Warboss, while the enduring clans, six of them great, cut across every tribe. All Orks give off a low level of psychic energy, and when a Warlord grows mighty this shared charge draws whole tribes together, swelling into a Waaagh!, a war of conquest that continues until final defeat. Mekboyz manufacture the Orks' weapons, and their kustom improvements often carry hidden flaws; Weirdboyz vent the gathered psychic power of the mob in destructive blasts.

Chaos is the power of the warp, ruled by four great gods: Khorne the Blood God, Tzeentch the Great Sorcerer, Nurgle the Lord of Decay and Slaanesh the Lord of Pleasure. During the Horus Heresy nine Space Marine Legions rebelled with Horus; defeated, the Traitor Legions fled into the Eye of Terror and remain there ten thousand years on. Each Legion keeps its own character, and its Champions bear the gifts and mutations of the gods they serve. When a great Champion unites the Eye, its hordes pour out: daemons, Cultists and Beastmen marching behind the Chaos Space Marines.

The Tyranids are an alien race from beyond the galaxy, and they strip the worlds they reach of every living thing. Each Tyranid is an organism created for a specific function, from the living ships of the hive fleets to weapons that are themselves symbiote creatures. No Tyranid possesses a mind of its own; every one is a small part of the hive mind, a single intelligence directing the entire race. Large creatures such as Tyranid Warriors and Hive Tyrants relay the hive mind's will to the lesser broods around them, and steer the swarms towards fresh genetic material.

The Squats descend from human miners who settled the high-gravity worlds of the galactic core and were then cut off for millennia by warp storms. Isolation and heavy gravity made them a shorter, tougher people with their own civilisation. They live in Strongholds built over mine workings; every Stronghold is independent, most belong to one of the seven hundred Leagues, and the Guilds carry engineering knowledge between all. Every Squat is trained to fight in the Stronghold's Brotherhood, and generations of tunnel war have made them resolute close-quarter fighters; the oldest develop psychic powers and are revered as Ancestor Lords.

The Sisters of Battle are the Orders Militant of the Adepta Sororitas, the fighting arm of the Adeptus Ministorum, the Ecclesiarchy of the Imperial creed. The Decree Passive forbids the Ecclesiarchy any "men under arms"; the all-female Daughters of the Emperor fell outside its wording and were taken into the church as its one permitted army. The Orders are governed from two Convents, one on Terra and one on Ophelia VII. Battle Sisters fight in power armour with boltguns, trained also on special weapons such as the flamer, and a squad may celebrate one of the Sacred Rites before battle.

The Necrons are the warriors of the Necrontyr, a civilisation believed to have vanished some sixty million years ago, leaving little behind but ruined tomb-temples on dead worlds. They appear without warning as raiding forces of metal figures built in imitation of the human skeleton, and lay waste to outposts, colonies and whole cities. Their guns flay a target away a layer at a time; their machinery erases records and disables equipment, so a raid leaves neither witness nor evidence. A Necron struck down will often repair itself and rise again; one damaged beyond repair fades from view and vanishes.

The Ultramarines are a Space Marine Chapter of the First Founding, raised under the Primarch Roboute Guilliman, who wrote the Codex Astartes; no Chapter follows its precepts more closely, and the Ultramarines are commonly taken as the model of Codex organisation. From their fortress on Macragge they rule Ultramar, a realm of worlds that supports the Chapter directly in place of Imperial tithes. In the First Tyrannic War the First Company was destroyed holding Macragge's polar fortresses against Hive Fleet Behemoth; the Chapter retook the fortresses and cleared the planet. The present Master is Marneus Calgar, Lord of Ultramar.

The Blood Angels are a Space Marine Chapter of the First Founding, descended from the Primarch Sanguinius, slain by Horus, and recruited from Baal and its moons. The dying memories of Sanguinius are encoded in the Chapter's gene-seed as a flaw. A Blood Angel overcome by the Black Rage is thrown back into the Primarch's final battle; such warriors form the Death Company, which fights in black armour under the Chapter's Chaplains, seeking death in battle. Survivors risk the Red Thirst, a hunger for blood. The Sanguinary Priests keep the preserved blood of Sanguinius in the Red Grail.

The Dark Angels were the first of the Space Marine Legions and are the most secretive of Chapters. When the Horus Heresy ended, the Dark Angels left on Caliban were turned against the Legion by Luther, the Primarch Lion El'Jonson's second-in-command; the world was destroyed, and the traitors, the Fallen, were scattered through space and time. The Chapter lives aboard the Rock, the surviving fragment of Caliban, and hunts the Fallen, bringing captives to repentance or death. Only those raised to the Inner Circle learn the truth. The Deathwing fights in Terminator armour; the Ravenwing rides bikes and land speeders.

The Space Wolves are a Space Marine Chapter of the First Founding, descended from the Primarch Leman Russ. Their fortress, the Fang, stands on the ice world of Fenris, whose warrior tribes supply the Chapter's recruits. In place of the Codex Astartes the Chapter divides into twelve Great Companies, each under a Wolf Lord answerable only to the Great Wolf. Every recruit absorbs the Canis gene helix, which carries the curse of the Wulfen. Warriors fight in packs graded by age, from the young Blood Claws through the proven Grey Hunters to the older Long Fangs with their heavy weapons.

A Genestealer Cult begins when a Genestealer plants its seed in a human host. The victim becomes a Brood Brother, bound to the brood's psychic will, and the offspring of the implanted are Hybrids, part alien and part human. Over generations the Cult spreads through a world's society, its most human members infiltrating the government and defence forces. The Patriarch, the first and oldest Genestealer, holds the brood together; the near-human Magus speaks and acts on its behalf. The brood emits a psychic signal that draws a Tyranid hive fleet, and when the fleet nears, the Cult rises in revolt.
